# @vllnt/convex-flags

> Convex component for feature flags in TypeScript: kill switches, variants, attribute targeting, percentage rollouts, per-subject overrides and React hooks.

Install `@vllnt/convex-flags` (unreleased builds from `main` use the `canary`
dist-tag). Peer dependency `convex@^1.45.0`; `react@^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0` is
optional and only needed for `@vllnt/convex-flags/react`. Mount it with
`app.use(flags)` from `@vllnt/convex-flags/convex.config` and call it through
`new Flags(components.flags)` from host queries, mutations and actions.
Management methods: `define` (full replace), `update` (partial), `enable`,
`disable`, `archive`, `restore`, `remove`, `setOverride`, `clearOverride`.
Read methods: `get`, `list`, `evaluate`, `variant`, `isEnabled`, `all`. A flag
is keyed by an opaque host string and its value is `boolean | string | number`.
Evaluation order: per-subject override, archived (serves the base value with
reason `disabled`), targeting rules in order, flag-level rollout, base value.
Rollouts bucket by the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of `<flag key>:<subject>`, where the
subject is `subjectRef` or the `by` attribute. An unknown key returns the
caller `default` (reason `default`) or `false` (reason `unknown`) and never
throws. `update`, `enable`, `disable`, `archive`, `restore`, `remove` and
`setOverride` throw a plain `Error` whose message contains `FLAG_NOT_FOUND` for
a key that does not exist (`define` creates it, `clearOverride` does nothing);
empty keys or subject refs and `NaN`, infinite or negative weights throw
`ConvexError` with `data.code` `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `all` fails while any key
starts with `$`, has a character outside printable ASCII or exceeds 1024
characters; use printable ASCII keys. React hooks `useFlag` and
`useFlags` take the host's own public queries. The host owns auth and the
meaning of keys, subjects and attributes.

## When to use

- Use it when a Convex app needs on/off switches it can flip without a deploy.
- Use it when a feature goes to a percentage of users, or to users whose
  attributes match rules, and each user must keep the same value.
- Use it when clients must see a flag change live through a Convex query.
- Do not use it when you run an A/B experiment and need sticky assignments and
  exposure counts per variant: use `@vllnt/convex-experiments`.
- Do not use it when you need to measure what a flagged feature did (events,
  funnels, retention): use `@vllnt/convex-analytics`.

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in the package at `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-flags/docs/`
and match the installed version. Read them, and the shipped `src/`, before
writing code. The links below to `./` paths are files inside the installed package.
